alt: A log-log plot of how often each word of the novel War and Peace appears against its frequency rank: a few words are very common and most words are rare, following a straight line (Zipf's law).
author: Cosmia Nebula

alt: The Google Books Ngram Viewer line chart for the two-word n-gram 'data science', showing how its frequency in the Google Books English corpus changes from 1800 to 2000.
author: Jasraj Raghuwanshi

alt: A poem in which every word is a real English word but many are the wrong word (Eye, Pea Sea, plane lee, knot sea), so a dictionary spell checker underlines only 'chequer'.
author: Jerrold H. Zar

alt: A hidden Markov model: hidden states X1, X2, X3 with transition arrows a between them, and observed outputs y1 to y4 reached from each state through emission arrows b.
author: Tdunning

alt: A Viterbi trellis: five columns for five observations and five rows for five states, with every possible link drawn dotted and the single best state path (3, 2, 5, 3, 4) drawn as a thick line.
author: Enrique Benimeli

alt: Output of a part-of-speech tagger on 'displaCy uses JavaScript, SVG and CSS.': each word has its Penn Treebank tag below it (NN, VBZ, NNP, CC) and arcs show grammatical links between words.
author: Artichok3

alt: The sentence 'Barack Obama was born in Hawaii' labelled word by word in two tag schemes: B-PER and I-PER mark a person name, B-LOC a place, and O marks words outside any entity.
author: Arthur-Kunst

alt: A derivation (parse) tree of a context-free grammar: start symbol S at the root, non-terminals A and B inside, terminals a and b at the leaves, and an empty string epsilon at the bottom.
author: MartinThoma

alt: Two different parse trees for the same string x + y * z, one grouping (x + y) first and the other y * z first: the picture of an ambiguous grammar.
author: Pat Hawks

alt: The sentence 'Drunks could put off the customers.' drawn two ways: a dependency tree (top, words link directly to words) and a phrase-structure tree (bottom, with NP and VP groups).
author: Tjo3ya

alt: A hierarchy where Color is the hypernym, Purple, Red, Blue and Green are its hyponyms, Red and Blue are co-hyponyms, and Crimson, Violet and Lavender are hyponyms of Purple.
author: RXerself

alt: A semantic network: Cat, Bear and Whale 'is a' Mammal, Mammal 'is an' Animal, Mammal 'has' Vertebra, and Whale and Fish 'live in' Water.
author: Konstable

alt: Words drawn as points in a 2-D space: the arrow from France to Paris is parallel to the arrow from Germany to Berlin, so the same direction stands for the relation 'capital of'.
author: Fschwarzentruber

alt: The skip-gram idea: the centre word 'loves' is used to predict the words around it, 'the', 'man', 'his' and 'son', so words that share contexts end up with similar vectors.
author: Zhang, Lipton, Li and Smola (Dive into Deep Learning)
